cards.explanation: The answer is in his rivers. The lament says Pharaoh is like a monster in the seas, and then it says, "You thrash about in your rivers…" (Ezekiel 32:2). Those rivers are his own backyard, friends. A monster making a big scene in his own backyard is still a monster making a big scene.

The answer is False. Pharaoh doesn't keep anything clear. The lament says he is "…churning up the waters with your feet and muddying the streams." (Ezekiel 32:2). I've made a mess on my own counter before, friends, so I won't judge.

The answer is His net. The Lord GOD says, "I will spread My net over you…" (Ezekiel 32:3). Pharaoh was thrashing around like he owned the water, friends. Now God has a net out, and nobody thrashes his way out of that.

The answer is out in an open field. God says, "I will abandon you on the land and hurl you into the open field." (Ezekiel 32:4). The net draws him up out of the water, and he ends up on the land. An open field is where he gets left, friends, and that's a long way from the rivers he was thrashing around in.

The answer is True. God says, "I will cause all the birds of the air to settle upon you…" (Ezekiel 32:4). The birds are in the picture along with the beasts. It's a heavy part of the lament, friends, and I think it's meant to show how far Pharaoh has fallen.

The answer is False. It isn't one small spot at all, friends. God says, "I will put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains." (Ezekiel 32:5). Mountains and valleys cover a whole lot of ground.

The answer is that they go dark. God says, "I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light." (Ezekiel 32:7). He also says He will "…darken their stars." and bring darkness on Egypt's land (Ezekiel 32:7-8). Even the sky goes quiet over this fall, friends. When the lights go out up there, you know it's serious.

The answer is that they shudder in horror. God says, "…their kings will shudder in horror because of you when I brandish My sword before them." (Ezekiel 32:10). Pharaoh's fall shakes up many peoples and their kings. When something that big drops, friends, a lot of folks feel it.

The answer is the most ruthless of all nations. God says, "I will make your hordes fall by the swords of the mighty, the most ruthless of all nations." (Ezekiel 32:12). That's how the text itself describes them, friends. They're described by how hard they are, not how old or rich.

The answer is True. God says, "They will ravage the pride of Egypt and all her multitudes will be destroyed." (Ezekiel 32:12). Pride and multitudes both go down in that verse, friends. It's a big, sobering line.

The answer is False. God says, "No human foot will muddy them again, and no cattle hooves will disturb them." (Ezekiel 32:13). The stirring is over, friends, and that's a real change from the thrashing in verse 2. It's like a kitchen that finally goes quiet after the whole family leaves.
The word is settle. God says, "Then I will let her waters settle and will make her rivers flow like oil…" (Ezekiel 32:14). The waters settle, friends, and the rivers flow like oil.
The answer is that He is the LORD. God says, "…then they will know that I am the LORD." (Ezekiel 32:15). What comes to be known, friends, is who He is.

The answer is True. God says, "This is the lament they will chant for her; the daughters of the nations will chant it." (Ezekiel 32:16). The daughters of the nations are the ones who chant it, friends. A lament that big needs a big choir.
